title: Nonstationary finite-armed bandits: unknown mean-variation budget.
summary: A fixed sequence of bounded reward distributions may vary over time, and the learner observes only the selected arm's reward. One algorithm must adapt to every undisclosed budget; performance is evaluated using the actual environment's variance and mean variation. Different levels of budget knowledge cannot be interchanged.

model.instance: There are $K$ arms with rewards in $[0,1]$, independent across rounds. All reward laws and unknown means $\mu_{t,i}$ are fixed before interaction. Total mean drift is $$V_\mu=\sum_{t=2}^{T}\|\mu_t-\mu_{t-1}\|_\infty,\qquad \mu_t=(\mu_{t,1},\ldots,\mu_{t,K}).$$.

operations.query_signature: Choose arm $I_t$, then receive only its reward. Inputs $K,T$ are public; $V_\mu$, means, and change locations are hidden, and no nontrivial actual-drift bound is given. A single causal policy cannot take $V_\mu$ or a nontrivial bound on it as input. Past feedback may be stored and reused computationally; no additional historical or sample queries are available beyond the explicitly declared interface.
